title: Hastening: A Weekly Church Report - Meridian Magazine
text:
This week’s Hastening takes readers around the world—from a powerful message of hope following the passing of King Harald V to an exclusive look at the dramatic transformation of the Salt Lake Temple. Discover how Church leaders are bringing hope to earthquake survivors in Colombia, building a brighter future in Sierra Leone, and strengthening families in Peru. Plus, see a new temple take root in Idaho, witness the remarkable growth of Church education in West Africa, and learn what’s being done to preserve the Great Salt Lake and make youth camp planning easier.
ONE
In Mourning, the Church Shares a Message of Hope and Resurrection
Friday, August 28, 2026
The First Presidency
The First Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints released a statement following the passing of His Majesty King Harald V. READ THE STATEMENT HERE .
TWO
Behind the Spires: CNN Reveals the Salt Lake Temple’s Historic Transformation
Saturday, August 29, 2026
Salt Lake Temple
CNN, a major United States-based media outlet, has published a story on the renovation of the iconic Salt Lake Temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints just days before ticket distribution begins for a six-month celebration starting in April and running through October 1, 2027. READ STORY HERE .
THREE
Elder Stevenson Brings Hope to Colombia Earthquake Survivors
Saturday, August 29, 2026
Apostolic Ministry
In the wake of a recent earthquake that struck southwest Colombia, Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints met on Monday, August 24, 2026, with Santiago de Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder to review ongoing emergency aid and discuss long-term recovery for affected families. Church members, mental health professionals and local volunteers have mobilized across Cali — a critical healthcare hub for the region — to deliver food kits, assist at collection centers, and provide emotional support to survivors. READ STORY HERE .
FOUR
Building a Brighter Future: Elder Gilbert Meets with Sierra Leone Leaders
Thursday, August 27, 2026
Apostolic Ministry
In his first visit as an Apostle of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints to Sierra Leone, Elder Clark G. Gilbert met with His Excellency Vice President Mohamed Juldeh Jalloh in Freetown on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. Much of their conversation focused on ways the Church of Jesus Christ and the Sierra Leone government can improve the country’s education. READ STORY HERE .
FIVE
Hope for the Great Salt Lake: The Church Calls for Conservation and Cooperation
Wednesday, August 26, 2026
To All The World
We are mindful of the many weather-related disasters and other hardships suffered by people across the world. While our concern is global, we refer in this statement to the extended drought in parts of the western United States, and specifically its impact on Utah’s Great Salt Lake. READ STORY HERE.
SIX
A New Temple Takes Root in Idaho
Saturday, August 29, 2026
Temples Rising
A groundbreaking ceremony was held for the Coeur d’Alene Idaho Temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on Saturday, August 29, 2026.
Elder Hutch U. Fale of the United States West Area Presidency presided at the event. During the program, several speakers shared their testimonies of the temple and their relationships with Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ. READ STORY HERE .
SEVEN
Strengthening Families, Serving Communities: Elder Stevenson Visits Peru’s President
Friday, August 28, 2026
Apostolic Ministry
Elder Gary E. Stevenson met with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori Higuchi on Thursday, August 27, 2026, at the Government Palace in Lima. During the meeting, Elder Stevenson conveyed greetings from the Church’s First Presidency and described the faith’s worldwide mission to help individuals live the gospel of Jesus Christ, care for those in need and strengthen families and communities. He noted that Church members are encouraged to support and sustain their governments, obey the laws of the land and contribute positively to their neighborhoods, schools and civic life. READ STORY HERE .
EIGHT
Opening Doors: Church Education Transforms Lives in West Africa
Sunday, August 30, 2026
Church Education
In 2011, a small group of students in Accra gathered around a single computer as BYU–Pathway began taking root in Ghana and was the first Pathway cohort outside of the United States. Today, a new Global Education Center (GEC) in Accra is under construction and will house more than 100 computers — a stark contrast that illustrates a dramatic expansion of Church education across West Africa. READ STORY AND WATCH VIDEO HERE.
NINE
Planning Youth Camp Just Got Easier
Thursday, August 27, 2026
Chosen Generation
Beginning in the fall of 2026, the process for reserving one of the 155 recreational properties owned by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in the United States and Canada will become simpler, provide better support for combined youth programs, and offer greater flexibility for leaders. READ STORY AND LEARN MORE HERE .
